_comment: Catalog of the model providers and plans this project can use. 'env' lists the names of the keys a provider needs (values live outside the repository, in state/providers.env). 'set' maps a key onto the variables a worker tool reads. 'automation' says whether the plan's terms allow unattended, scripted runs: only 'yes' entries belong in config/routing.json. 'checked' is the date the facts were read from the provider's own pages; re-check before paying. Prices are the published list prices on that date.

anthropic-subscription.name: Claude subscription (Claude Code sign-in)
anthropic-subscription.use: Tiers A and B. The scarce resource: architect, leads, high-risk review. Never bulk reading.
anthropic-subscription.notes: Used by the claude runner when no provider is named. Models are chosen per session with --model (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable) and --effort.

opencode-go.name: OpenCode Go
opencode-go.use: Tier C default once a model is chosen: flat-fee access to several open-weight coding models through OpenCode.
opencode-go.price: 10 USD per month; Plus 40 USD per month; limits are dollar budgets per 5 hours, week and month
opencode-go.notes: Connected with `opencode auth login -p opencode-go` (key kept by OpenCode in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json). Limits per model: 5-hour window = 20% of the monthly allowance, weekly = 50%. Largest allowances (Go plan, monthly / est. requests per 5 h): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $100 / 43,300; MiMo-V2.6-Flash $60 / 30,100; Hy4 $60 / 2,710; Kimi K2.7 Code $60 / 994; Qwen4 Max $15 / 463; DeepSeek V4 Pro $15 / 1,040. Hy4 Flash Free is unlimited for a limited time. On a limit the dispatcher marks the model limited (state/limits.json) and moves to the next candidate. Go is for coding-agent traffic through OpenCode, which sends the session id Go requires.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek API
deepseek.use: Tier C: bulk desktop study and routine implementation at token prices.
deepseek.notes: Standard API, so scripted use is normal. Check the provider's data-retention terms against SECURITY-NOTICE.md before sending source.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.use: Any tier: one key for many models, useful for escalation and for comparing models on the same packet.
openrouter.notes: OpenCode reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the environment. Model ids look like openrouter/<vendor>/<model>.

anthropic-compatible.name: Any Anthropic-compatible endpoint driven by the claude runner
anthropic-compatible.use: Tier C with the Claude Code tool but a cheaper model behind it.
anthropic-compatible.notes: The two DC_ variables keep the endpoint away from the supervisor's own Claude session: the dispatcher sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL only inside the worker process.

alibaba-coding-plan.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio Coding Plan
alibaba-coding-plan.use: Interactive sessions only (a person at the terminal, for example in a herdr pane). Not for the dispatcher.
alibaba-coding-plan.price: Pro 50 USD per month: 6,000 requests per 5 hours, 45,000 per week, 90,000 per month. Lite is no longer sold.
alibaba-coding-plan.notes: The plan's terms prohibit automated scripts and non-interactive use and name suspension as the consequence. Endpoints: OpenAI-compatible https://coding-intl.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1 and Anthropic-compatible https://coding-intl.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/apps/anthropic. For scripted Qwen use, take a pay-as-you-go Model Studio key instead and add it as its own provider.

openai-codex.name: Codex CLI with a ChatGPT plan or an OpenAI API key
openai-codex.use: Tier B: independent review by a different model family, and hard implementation.
openai-codex.notes: Sign in once with 'codex login'. For API-key runs set CODEX_API_KEY in state/providers.env. OpenAI's guide says not to use the ChatGPT-sign-in automation flow for public repositories in CI.

candidatesNotYetEvaluated: OpenCode Zen (pay-as-you-go model gateway from the OpenCode team)
Alibaba Model Studio pay-as-you-go and Token Plan
